name: Kodaikanal
description: Kodaikanal is a hill station at roughly 2,100 metres in the Palani Hills, best known for its cool climate, a star-shaped lake at its centre, and shola forests laced with walking trails. It suits quiet nature lovers and families seeking relief from the plains heat, though the town itself is touristy and traffic-choked in peak season — honest visitors plan walks early and avoid weekends in April and May.
nearest_railhead: Kodai Road (80 km from Kodaikanal Town; the nearest railhead on the Chennai–Madurai line)
nearest_airport: Madurai Airport (120 km; nearest commercial airport with regular domestic connections)

attractions.name: Kodaikanal Lake
attractions.description: A manmade, star-shaped lake at the heart of town, built in 1863. Walking, cycling, or taking a pedal boat around its 5 km periphery is pleasant at a measured pace, though the lakeside promenade is crowded with vendors and tourists on weekends.

attractions.name: Coaker's Walk
attractions.description: A 1 km paved cliff-edge promenade offering sweeping views of the Palani Hills and the plains below when skies are clear — which is far from guaranteed. A small telescope observatory at one end charges a nominal fee; the walk is short, flat, and easily done by seniors.

attractions.name: Pillar Rocks
attractions.description: Three vertical granite pillars rising about 122 metres from the valley floor, viewable from a fenced platform. The site is atmospheric in morning mist but often fully socked in by cloud by midday; the short path from the road is paved and manageable.

attractions.name: Bryant Park
attractions.description: A well-maintained botanical garden adjoining the lake, established in 1908 and notable for its rose garden and greenhouse collection. It is a gentle, cultivated space rather than a wild landscape; worth an hour if you enjoy horticulture, otherwise skippable.

attractions.name: Dolphin's Nose
attractions.description: A flat rock outcrop projecting over a sheer drop with a panoramic view of the Pambar Valley. Getting here requires a 2 km walk each way on a forest trail from the road at Liril Falls, which adds light physical effort; the viewpoint itself is genuinely dramatic.

attractions.name: Bear Shola Falls
attractions.description: A modest seasonal waterfall about 2 km from the town centre, accessible by a short unpaved path. Flow is reliable only after the monsoon; in summer it can be barely a trickle. Primarily a pleasant shaded walk through a small shola patch rather than a dramatic waterfall.

attractions.name: Perumal Peak Trek
attractions.description: The highest point in the Palani Hills at 2,467 m, reached by a moderately demanding 7 km trail through shola forest and grassland. The summit offers 360-degree views and is far less crowded than the town-centre viewpoints; a forest department permit is required.

attractions.name: Berijam Lake
attractions.description: A pristine reservoir 21 km from Kodaikanal town, surrounded by dense shola forest and managed as a protected catchment — entry requires a Forest Department permit and visitor numbers are strictly capped. The drive through the Palani Hills reserve and the stillness of the lake make this the most genuinely unspoiled spot accessible from Kodaikanal.

attractions.name: Shembaganur Museum of Natural History
attractions.description: A small natural history museum run by the Sacred Heart College (a Jesuit institution), housing an orchid collection with over 300 Palani Hills species and wildlife specimens. It is genuinely educational, unhurried, and almost entirely overlooked by mainstream tourists — a legitimate hidden gem for nature-curious visitors.

attractions.name: Kukkal Caves
attractions.description: A cluster of prehistoric cave shelters with megalithic burial urns at Kukkal village, roughly 25 km from town. The site is rarely visited, requires a guide and some scrambling, and offers genuine archaeological interest alongside grassland views — a true off-the-beaten-path half-day for curious travellers.
